title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (August 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: the publisher's standing rule, restated on conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200) -- "The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index (R) at 10 a.m. ET on the last Tuesday of every month." 2027-08-31 is the last Tuesday of August 2027. The rule is corroborated for AUGUST specifically by three of the publisher's own dated next-release lines, each read this session off a July edition fetched direct 2026-09-06 at HTTP 200 and verified against its own "Source: July <year> Consumer Confidence Survey" line rather than trusted by slug: CCI-July-2022 (644,517 bytes) "The next release is Tuesday, August 30 at 10 AM ET", CCI-July-2023 (1,528,271 bytes) "Tuesday, August 29", CCI-July-2024 (1,015,724 bytes) "Tuesday, August 27th" -- each of which is the last Tuesday of its August. A fourth August, 2026-08-25, is the release date of the edition currently live on the publisher's landing page and is likewise the last Tuesday of its month. No August-2027 announcement exists yet, so this is the publisher's rule applied forward against a verified August record rather than a posted date. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the consumer-confidence-2027-07-27 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06), one edition forward on the same chain, and proposed for one measured reason rather than to keep the chain rolling: IT IS THE CONTROL THIS CHAIN NOW NEEDS. This session established that a collision with FOMC day one is a property of WHICH MONTH the Fed's non-SEP meeting falls in -- every day one landing in January, April, July or October is the last Tuesday of that month, 22 of 22 across 2021-2027, while the SEP meetings sit 7 to 21 days earlier and never collide (0 of 28). The direct consequence is that the July print has never once been observed clean (0 of 6) and the chain's 51-day clean-CB-day baseline holds ZERO July and ZERO January observations. August is the adjacent month that is clean 6 of 6, sits in the same 9-of-9 summer volatility block the 06-29 sibling measured (Jun+Jul+Aug vs the rest of the year, SPY and VIX both p<0.0001), and is the SECOND month of its quarter -- the position whose FIRST four sessions run 5 of 9 WIDER than non-month-start sessions (AMZN p<0.0001, AAPL 0.0020, TLT 0.0231, XLF 0.0241, XRT 0.0369) while its last four are 0 of 9. So an August print is the same season and the same publisher with the collision removed, which is the only way this chain gets a within-summer contrast. Two cautions for whichever lane takes it. FIRST, do not borrow July's cut-off lag: July's own are 5/6/8 days (2022-07-21, 2023-07-19, 2024-07-22), the widest within-month spread in the chain, and the current August 2026 edition states a survey period of "August 3-16" against an 08-25 release, a 9-day lag longer than anything July shows -- the lag varies BETWEEN months and WITHIN them, so project a range and never a point. SECOND, the chain's standing premise that no sourced edition has printed Expectations at or above the Board's 80.0 recession threshold is REFUTED as of this session: CCI-July-2023 printed 88.3, "well above 80", and no US recession followed in 2023. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
